witness_description: Let K be the algebraic closure of Q, let V=K^1, and let H consist only of the 1-by-1 identity matrix.
refutation_explanation: The singleton H is a Zariski-closed subgroup of GL(V), cut out by x_11-1=0, and H^0=H. Its action on the one-dimensional V is irreducible, and its sole element fixes every nonzero vector. But H has one element, while PSL(2,K) has at least two: the classes of I_2 and diag(2,1/2) are distinct modulo {I_2,-I_2}. Hence H is not PSL(2).
search_space: Exhaustively swept the five candidates (K^n,{I_n}) for integers n=1,2,3,4,5, in increasing n order; the n=1 candidate is a counterexample.
